The passkey-login assertion becomes vacuous — it passes even if the clickAuthenticate() login silently fails and the appPage check is satisfied by residual state — weakening the only verification that the external-key passkey re-auth flow actually produces the expected login event.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The challenge() error path inverts the old user-null condition: previously webauthn data was filled exactly when context.getUser() == null, now fillContextForm is skipped for the fresh-login error case because isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null. A user on an initial (non-re-auth) login whose context.getUser() is null when the challenge is re-rendered (e.g. a failed credential attempt before the user is bound to the context) loses the passkey/conditional-UI form entirely after a typo, leaving password-only recovery where the old code kept the passkey option; no test in the diff covers webauthn form presence on a first-login error with user unset.
records.rationale:
The diff shows an explicit condition inversion in UsernamePasswordForm’s error challenge path. Previously, on error it called webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) when context.getUser() == null and passkeys were enabled:

- old: `if (context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()) { webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context); }`

Now it only fills when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, and that helper requires `user != null`:

- new: `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())) { webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context); }`

records.issue_text: [BUG] The webauthn setup moved out of the user==null branch in authenticate() and is now gated on user != null, so on a fresh login (no user identified yet) fillContextForm is no longer invoked from authenticate(), inverting the prior behavior where conditional-UI setup happened precisely when the user was not selected. The initial username/password page for a passkeys-enabled realm no longer gets the WebAuthn conditional-UI attribute set from this call site; the fresh-login passkey autofill only survives if some other uncovered call site (the formData challenge overload) fills it, and any regression there is invisible to the diff's tests which only assert webauthn form presence at fresh login in one scenario.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] UsernameForm.authenticate now skips the user-set shortcut whenever passkeys are enabled, unconditionally invoking the username form during re-authentication, and the isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() call reads realm policy without any per-user credential check, so the presented form's security posture depends on the WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()==false override to avoid leaking a re-auth user's registered authenticator list via fillContextForm. If a custom deployment swaps WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator for the base WebAuthnAuthenticator in the conditional-passkeys flow, the base class's shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators (user != null) returns true during re-auth and fillContextForm enumerates the victim user's registered WebAuthn credential list (labels/AAGUIDs) to the login page, giving an unauthenticated observer fingerprinting info that was previously only shown post-identification.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff inverts the condition for filling webauthn data on the initial username/password page from `context.getUser() == null` (anonymous, pre-selection) to `user != null` (post-selection), and no test in this diff asserts the presence or absence of the webauth conditional-UI form on the anonymous first page of the UsernamePasswordForm flow. If fillContextForm on the anonymous page is needed for the browser's conditional-mediation autofill to trigger before the user types a username, that regression ships undetected: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey types the username and checks the webauth form only after the user is already selected (and the Organization test was updated to the new post-selection expectation), so the no-user path has zero coverage. Test files checked: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java.
